restatement.intent: Every artefact an agent, program or person produces carries, from the moment it is created, a record of what made it and what it read; every judgement passed on it is appended, never edited, and current state is derived by folding that log.
restatement.problem: When artefacts do not record their maker and decisions overwrite one another, no source can be measured, filtered, audited or undone without destroying the evidence.
restatement.solution: Split into two halves that are usually adopted together but are separable. (1) A stamper on every creating path attaches a provenance record to each artefact: maker kind and ids, inputs with hashes, code/model version, time — inline or as a sidecar. (2) Every decision about an artefact is an appended event (accept, reject, correct, undo) with actor, time and reason; one shared fold function turns the log (overlaid on the artefacts) into current state, and queries run both ways: what made this, and what did this source make.

quiz.answer: What made it (maker kind plus identifiers, inputs with hashes, version, time) and who decided what about it (the appended decision events).
A rejection is information: without it the acceptance rate of a source cannot be computed, and the same rejected suggestion may be offered again.
Review events record item, decision and time but not the reviewer — enough with one reviewer, not with two. The chapter's advice is to add the actor before it is needed.
The corrections went into a review log of decisions; scoring scripts fold that log over the gold labels at scoring time, so the original labels stay intact and the correction is itself traceable.

transfer.why: Two maker kinds (people, agent sessions) produce the same kind of artefact, results must be measured per source (revert rates) and one faulty source version must be listable wholesale — exactly the applicability conditions. The hard part is granularity: 'which lines' needs per-item origin, not per-commit origin.

participants.Provenance record: commit (ideally hunk) stamp: kind person|agent, ids {session, model, promptVersion, step}, inputs = files read plus lockfile hashes, base revision, time
participants.Stamper: one helper called from every commit path: agent commit tool, human CLI wrapper, merge bot, cherry-pick/rebase automation
participants.Schema: fixed trailer keys and definitions (what counts as model version, prompt version, 'line authored by'), so the three queries agree on units
participants.Decision event: revert, force-push correction, review approval; itemId = commit sha
participants.Decision log: append-only table or notes ref keyed by sha, written by the revert bot and reviewers, not by the authors
participants.Fold: single function mapping sha → current decision plus surviving line ranges, shared by the revert dashboard, blame/blame-like view and CI
participants.Lineage queries: madeBy(promptVersion) → all commits and lines from that prompt; sourceOf(line); revertRate(source)

transfer.sketch:
value Provenance: kind (person | agent), ids: {session, model, prompt, step},
                  inputs: [(path, hash)], base, at

commit(repo, diff, ctx) → sha
  sha = git.commit(diff, msg ++ trailer(Provenance(ctx.kind, {session: ctx.run, model: ctx.model,
            prompt: ctx.promptVersion, step: ctx.step},
            inputs: [(f, hash(f)) for f in ctx.readFiles] ++ [(lockfile, hash(lockfile))],
            base: head(repo), at: now())))
  write(notes/lineage, sha, provenance)      -- sidecar, commit format unchanged

revert(sha, actor, reason) → ok
  append(log, Event(sha, revert, actor, now(), reason))

fold(events) → map sha → Event            -- the one function
  state = {}
  for e in events sorted by log sequence:  -- not by wall clock
    match e.decision:
      undo → state = minus(state, e.itemId)
      _    → state = state ⊕ {e.itemId: e}
  return state

madeBy(prompt) → [c for c in commits if c.provenance.ids.prompt == prompt]
revertRate(source) → count(revert, source) / count(decided, source)
key_notes: Note 2 (origin per item) matters most: commit-level stamps decay to file or repo level after squash merges and rebases, so 'which agent session wrote which lines' requires hunk/line records, not just a commit trailer.

Note 1 (stamp in every creating path): the paths here are numerous — agent tool, human CLI, merge bot, cherry-pick, automated formatting commits — and an unstamped commit is silently dropped by madeBy and undercounts revert rates.
Note 5 (write the fold once): three consumers already exist (revert dashboard, blame view, CI), which is precisely the dust three-folds situation.
Note 9 (hash inputs that may change): prompt files and dependency lockfiles must be hashed, otherwise 'prompt version 3' names a file that no longer exists.
Note 8 (sidecar when the format must not change): a commit trailer plus a notes ref keeps `git log` readable by existing tooling.
transfer.risk: Provenance collapsing at merge time: one squashed or rebased commit turns a hundred agent-authored lines into a single human-authored commit, so the revert-rate-by-source number silently becomes wrong rather than unavailable.

transfer.why: The proposed version fails the chapter's own do-not-use clause: the actor on every decision is the exact field the legal rule forbids, and several of the pattern's payoff queries (acceptance by source, error by source, madeBy a reviewer) are defined in terms of it. Only a reduced form fits.
key_notes: Applicability, third do-not-use bullet ('privacy rules forbid recording who did what; record only what the rules allow, and say so') is the governing clause; the reduced pattern records study, protocol version, AI triage model version and inputs as provenance, and appends decisions with the actor field absent or a per-session blind token that cannot be re-linked.
Note 6 ('add the actor before it is needed') is explicitly the wrong advice here and should not be applied.
Note 7 (definitions and units in the schema) still carries weight: the audit will ask what 'peer review complete' means.

Note 10 (corrections overlay, never rewrite) still applies to corrected reads, but the correction event must also be actor-free, and coarse timestamps are needed because wall-clock time plus a duty roster re-identifies the radiologist.
transfer.risk: Recording time, study and reviewer 'pseudonymously' and calling it anonymous: in a department of thirty with a published roster, timestamp plus pseudonym re-identifies, so the pattern quietly violates the requirement it was meant to satisfy.

review_notes.note: Two patterns are welded together: cheap creation-time provenance stamping, and the much heavier append-only decision log with a shared fold. They have different costs and different do-not-use conditions, so a reader cannot tell which half to adopt, and the do-not-use list answers only for a mix of both.
review_notes.suggestion: State explicitly that the two halves are separable, and give each its own trigger: stamp always when artefacts have multiple maker kinds; add the log only when decisions get revised and must be undone.

review_notes.note: The sketch does not implement the chapter's own solution. `fold(events) → map itemId → Event` takes only events, but note 10's overlay folds the review log over the gold labels, so artefacts are a second input. `undo` as `delete state[itemId]` makes the pre-undo state unreachable and contradicts 'never lose history'. And `acceptance(bySource)` divides accepted by decided per confidence band, but nothing joins an event to a suggestion's confidence band — that lives on the suggestion's provenance, not on the Event.
review_notes.suggestion: Write `fold(events, artefacts) → State` with an explicit as-of parameter, keep undo as an entry in the state (a view, not a deletion), and show the join that attaches confidence band to each decided item.

review_notes.note: `save` writes the artefact and then writes the provenance sidecar; a crash between the two leaves a permanently unstamped artefact, which is the exact failure note 1 warns about, and `path ++ ".provenance.json"` silently collides when many small artefacts land in one directory.
review_notes.suggestion: Stamp to a temp file and rename both, or write the provenance record first and let the artefact reference it; use a hashed sidecar path or a single directory-level index.

review_notes.note: Note 5 worries about folds disagreeing on an unknown decision or a malformed line, but the far likelier disagreement is order: events carry only `at: now()`, and wall clocks across machines reorder concurrent appends, so two folds can produce different state from the same log.
review_notes.suggestion: Give events a monotonic sequence number (log offset or Lamport clock) and have the shared fold sort by it; demote `at` to a display field.

review_notes.note: The Applicability list says to drop actor when privacy rules forbid it, while note 6 states unconditionally 'Add the actor before it is needed.' The advice contradicts itself with no cross-reference, and note 6 is the one a reader will follow.
review_notes.suggestion: Qualify note 6 with the privacy exception and say what to record instead (pseudonymous actor, coarse time, actor held in a separately access-controlled store).

review_notes.note: Four of ten notes open with project specifics (dust's Go scripts, the fitted radius, GCV-006, goja-cv cache keys); note 7 duplicates Chapter 2 and does not really belong here. The general rule gets buried and the chapter reads longer than the pattern needs.
review_notes.suggestion: Lead each note with the rule, keep one clause of evidence, and cut note 7 to a cross-reference.

review_notes.note: The same content — stamp at creation, append decisions, fold once, query both ways — is stated four times in near-identical wording before the Sketch, so a reader covers the same ground four times to reach the mechanics.
review_notes.suggestion: Keep Solution as the single statement and reduce Structure to the participant table; drop the repeated enumerations in Collaborations to the parts that add mechanics (the join for confidence bands, the undo path).

review_notes.note: Append-only logs cannot honour an erasure request: there is no way to remove a person's decisions from a log whose whole value is that it is never edited. The chapter mentions only 'record only what the rules allow'.
review_notes.suggestion: Add the escape hatches: tombstoning the payload while keeping the sequence position, or cryptographic erasure with per-subject keys.

review_notes.note: Reproducibility is claimed as a consequence, but the record lists inputs and code version only. A fold over a log reproduces state; reproducing the artefact also needs seeds, environment and dependency versions, none of which the provenance record names.
review_notes.suggestion: Add seeds, dependency lockfile hash and environment id to the recommended record, or narrow the consequence claim to 'audit and partially reproduce'.

ratings.comment: The provenance half is broadly and cheaply applicable and well argued; clarity and reusability are held back by merging it with the decision-log half, by a fold sketch that contradicts the text, and by advice that contradicts itself on recording the actor.
